qt: to the Commission Petros Kokkalis (Verts/ALE) Subject:

Following the devastating floods that hit Thessaly last September, the master plan for water management in the region1is now under public consultation. The plan ignores ecosystem services for climate proofing and protecting water resources and instead focuses on big construction projects, including 23 medium-sized and large dams, river deepening projects, the deforestation of riparian vegetation, the construction of 130 km of new dykes and the diversion of Achelous River. Considering: (a) the fact that on 13 March the Commission referred Greece to the ECJ2 for its failure to finalise the revision of its river basin management plans as required under the Water Framework Directive3 and of its flood risk management plans as required under the Floods Directive4; (b) the objections expressed by global environmental organisations5; and (c)the establishment of the for-profit Thessaly Water Management Association SA6, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Are the proposed master plan and the establishment of the new association in line with EU law and specifically with Directives 2000/60/EC and 2007/60/EC?

Does it not agree that, as required under Directive 2001/42/EC, a strategic environmental impact assessment should be carried out before any interventions begin in the region, given that environmental impacts are not provided for in the plan’s timeline?

at: (English version) to the Commission Petros Kokkalis (Verts/ALE) (10 April 2024) Subject: Master plan for water management in Thessaly Following the devastating floods that hit Thessaly last September, the master plan for water management in the regio n (1)is now under public consultation. The plan ignores ecosystem services for climate proofing and protecting water resources and instead focuses on big construction projects, including 23 medium-sized and large dams, river deepening projects, the deforestation of riparian vegetation, the construction of 130 km of new dykes and the diversion of Achelous River. Considering: (a) the fact that on 13 March the Commission referred Greece to the ECJ (2) for its failure to finalise the revision of its river basin management plans as required under the Water Framework Directiv e (3) and of its flood risk management plans as required under the Floods Directive (4); (b) the objections expressed by global environmental organisations (5); and (c)the establishment of the for-profit Thessaly Water Management Association SA (6), can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Are the proposed master plan and the establishment of the new association in line with EU law and specifically with Directives 2000/60/EC and 2007/60/EC?

Does it not agree that, as required under Directive 2001/42/EC, a strategic environmental impact assessment should be carried out before any interventions begin in the region, given that environmental impacts are not provided for in the plan’s timeline?

(13 June 2024) 1. The Commission has indeed launched legal proceedings against Greece in March 2024 (infringement case 2022/2191) for failure to communicate its River Basin Management Plans (RBMPs) and Flood Risk Management Plans in line with the provisions of the Water Framework Directive (7) (WFD) and of the Floods Directive (8) (FD). 2. Projects which might affect negatively the status of water bodies need to be included in the relevant RBMPs and be in compliance with relevant WFD’s provisions. It should be noted that in line with the FD, the objectives and measures regarding specifically the management of flood risks are determined at national level by the Member States, based on local and regional circumstances. Nevertheless, measures taken under the FD cannot run contrary to the objectives of the WFD. Member States are therefore responsible to ensure that any new project, also those of the masterplan — if and as eventually adopted by the Greek authorities — can only be authorised if in compliance with the conditions set out in the WFD. The application of the Strategic Environmental Assessment Directive (9) on the masterplan depends on whether the conditions of its Articles 2a and 3 are met. As regards specific projects or interventions related to water management or flood protection, next to heeding the provisions of the WFD, other EU environmental Directives would also apply, e.g., the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive (10).
